title: One gating convention, bounded waits, a default-deny egress boundary, and a known-offender lint for the Go test suite
planner_lane_reason: tools/launchd/derive-planner-lane.sh emits 'opus fail-closed:planner-lane-field-invalid' because the doc's line 8 reads 'Planner-Lane: codex-ok (mechanical Go test-infra work ...)' and the matcher requires the bare token. metadata.scope: Test-infrastructure hardening only - no language surface, no runtime behavior, no compiler change. Five parts: (1) one shared gating helper package (internal/testutil/gate.go + subproc.go) providing RequiresLiveNetwork, HangGuard, HangGuardContext and RunBounded; (2) migration of 5 substantive call sites (#583 gitcache live clone, #561 net_test live httpbin + new deterministic httptest coverage, #494 unbounded cmd/ailang subprocess helpers, #509 redundant absolute guardrail deleted, #587 60s hang-guard replaced by a warm-up run plus a derived bound) and deletion of 6 remaining inert testing.Short() gates; (3) internal/testutil/gatelint - a legibility lint for known offenders (R1 testing.Short, R2 Getenv(CI)/Getenv(GITHUB_ACTIONS), R3 narrow host list) that runs as a plain Go test on all CI legs, self-tested against fixtures every run; (4) the poisoned-proxy default-lane wiring (HTTP_PROXY=HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9, NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1, GOPROXY=off, preceded by an unpoisoned `go mod download all`) on ci.yml's two go test steps, build.yml's 4-entry matrix step and make/test.mk's $(GOTEST) line, each with an in-step env guard; (5) docs, CHANGELOG and issue closes.
metadata.non_scope: No -race in CI. No retry-on-failure. No generic third-party-host taint analysis. No OS-level egress blocking for the raw-TCP/SSH residual. No process-group grandchild cleanup on Windows. No unification of buildAilang with testutil.FindAilangBinary beyond adding a ctx bound. No replacement of the ollama probe-and-skip. No //go:build integration standardization. NO production HTTP client changes (specifically: do NOT add Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment to internal/effects/net.go). NO gatelint R4 for unbounded exec.Command (62 first-party test files would need seeding - recorded as Future Work with the measured count instead).
metadata.milestone_split_change_from_design_doc: CHANGED from 4 milestones to 5. The design doc's M3 bundles a ~460-LOC pure-Go linter (zero blast radius on dev) with the CI workflow edits (maximum blast radius on dev) in ONE commit. That is not bisectable and it violates the sprint's hard constraint that helpers/tests land first and the enforcement boundary lands last. Split: plan-M3 = gatelint + egress posture probe, pure Go, ZERO workflow files touched, revertable by deleting one directory plus one file; plan-M4 = the poison wiring, the ONLY commit touching .github/workflows/* or make/test.mk, one commit, six pre-commit gates, staged revert. Ordering M1 -> M2 -> M3 -> M4 -> M5 is fixed: M2 must precede M3 (TestGateLint_Repo scans the real tree), and M4 must be last (blast radius).
planner_refutations_and_new_hazards: REFUTED - V22 is wrong and AC3 is VACUOUS as written. The doc claims the poisoned-proxy command FAILS pre-sprint in internal/effects and builds AC3's whole non-vacuity argument on it. Measured at HEAD 9feefa3a6: `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 go test -count=1 -v ./internal/effects/ -run 'TestNetHttpPost|TestNetBodySizeLimit'` -> `ok github.com/sunholo-data/ailang/internal/effects 1.017s`, with `--- PASS: TestNetHttpPost/httpPost_to_httpbin.org (0.41s)`. Env control in the same block: CI=[unset] GITHUB_ACTIONS=[unset] SKIP_NET_TESTS=[unset], so the subtests were NOT skipped - they ran and reached the live internet THROUGH the poison. AC3 replaced by AC3a/AC3b/AC3c in the plan.

REFUTED (STRUCTURAL, root cause of the above) - the poisoned proxy is NOT a boundary for first-party HTTP. internal/effects/net.go:96,212,587, stream_ndjson.go:80 and stream_sse.go:70,329 construct bare &http.Transport{...} literals. A hand-built http.Transport has Proxy == nil (no proxy) unless Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment is set explicitly. Measured: `grep -rn -A6 'http\.Transport{' internal/effects/*.go | grep -c 'Proxy'` -> 0; `grep -rl 'ProxyFromEnvironment' --include='*.go' ./internal ./cmd | wc -l` -> 0; control `grep -rl 'http\.Transport{' --include='*.go' ./internal ./cmd | wc -l` -> 4. net.go additionally pins DialContext to a pre-validated IP (SSRF hardening) so it dials the target directly by construction. CONSEQUENCE: AILANG's own Net effect - the repo's principal HTTP client and the exact code path of #561 - is entirely outside the enforcement boundary. This is a LARGER hole than the doc's named raw-TCP residual because it is first-party code the repo owns and keeps adding tests for. The doc's Goals sentence 'Default go test ./... performs zero HTTP(S) egress - mechanically denied by the poisoned-proxy lane' is FALSE as written. NOT closed in this sprint (closing it is a production runtime change the doc disclaims, and would likely defeat the pinned-IP SSRF guard); documented in M5 and escalated to Mark.

HTTP_PROXY=... go test -count=1 $(go list ./... | grep -v /scripts)` -> rc=1, 105 ok, 30 no-test-files, and exactly ONE FAIL: internal/pkg (`--- FAIL: TestGitCache_Resolve_RealRepo`, `git clone failed ... exit status 128`). internal/effects PASSES under poison per the refutation above. metadata.budget_verdict: The design doc's 3-4 days is LOW. Realistic: 26h over ~4.5 executor-days. Four reasons: (1) M4 is not a 0.5-day task - its cost is not LOC but six sequential verification gates, two shell dialects for the same in-step guard, a `shell: bash` pin on a 4-leg matrix step whose current Windows behavior nobody has checked, an AC12 cold-cache drill that must run TWICE (negative control then the AC), and a CI round-trip; (2) the doc's own milestone split is not bisectable, so splitting gatelint from the workflow edits adds a commit boundary and a verification pass; (3) M2 grew by three items the doc did not scope - the AllowHTTP/AllowLocalhost discovery, the third unbounded helper at main_test.go:26, and a probable manual merge against PR #532; (4) calibration against recent same-shape sprints in this repo: M-RECORDED-STREAM-API-S1 730 LOC/3.75d, M-EVAL-STANDARD-CONFIDENCE-GATING 460 LOC/4d, M-MCP-EXACT-TOOL-SURFACE-LANE-B planned 1450 LOC/3.5d after its planner revised the doc's 17h to 25h. Raw 7-day velocity is `152 files changed, 11541 insertions(+), 1495 deletions(-)` on *.go, but that is aggregate across concurrent agents, not one executor's serial throughput; ~280 LOC/day of test-infrastructure-with-mandatory-falsification-drills is the honest per-executor rate. RECOMMENDATION: accept 26h / 4.5d and keep all ACs. If a hard 4-day box is required, the ONLY clean cut is deferring M5's doc work (-3h), accepting that the -short behavior change ships undocumented for a few days. Cutting M4's pre-commit gates instead is how dev goes red.
metadata.point_of_no_return: M4. It is the only commit that edits .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/build.yml and make/test.mk, and it changes the default posture of all 6 CI legs plus every developer's `make test` simultaneously. A mistake reds dev for every concurrent session and outranks the mission queue. Revert is `git revert --no-edit <M4-sha>` and must be staged before the push. M1, M2, M3 are all revertable in isolation with no cross-session effect: M1 adds a new package nothing imports yet; M2 changes only test files (a break is a named test failure); M3 adds a gate that runs on all 6 legs but touches zero workflow files.
controller_decisions_required: PR #532 vs M2 - #532 is CONFLICTING/DIRTY, open since 2026-07-29, and rewrites buildAilang (the exact helper M2 wraps) for a legitimate reason. Options: (a) land #532 first, then M2 wraps its sync.Once body in HangGuardContext; (b) M2 proceeds and #532 rebases onto it; (c) M2 absorbs #532's change. Planner recommends (a).

The R-B hole - does internal/effects/net.go get Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment? It would make the poison a genuine boundary for the repo's own HTTP client, but it is a production runtime behavior change the doc disclaims and would probably break the pinned-IP SSRF guard. Planner recommends NO in this sprint; document the hole and open a follow-up.

Should gatelint gain an R4 for unbounded exec.Command in *_test.go? 62 first-party test files have one; the sprint bounds 3. Planner recommends NOT in this sprint (an R4 with a 62-entry seed allowlist is a sprint of its own) but recording it as Future Work with the measured count.

The design doc needs correcting on V22, V30, the leg count, and its Goals paragraph. Whether that is a doc edit before execution or a note in the implementation report is the controller's call. Leaving V22 uncorrected risks an executor 'verifying' AC3 with a command that passes for the wrong reason.
